requirements.heading: Parameter and Response Lengths
requirements.text: Servers which support the CAPA command MUST support commands up to 255 octets.

requirements.heading: Parameter and Response Lengths
requirements.text: Servers MUST also support the largest maximum command length specified by any supported capability.

requirements.heading: The CAPA Command
requirements.text: A capability description MUST document in which states the capability is announced, and in which states the commands are valid.

requirements.heading: The CAPA Command
requirements.text: Capabilities available in the AUTHORIZATION state MUST be announced in both states.

requirements.heading: The CAPA Command
requirements.text: If a capability is announced in both states, but the argument might differ after authentication, this possibility MUST be stated in the capability description.

requirements.heading: The CAPA Command
requirements.text: If the authentication step negotiates an integrity protection layer, the client SHOULD reissue the CAPA command after authenticating, to check for active down-negotiation attacks.

requirements.heading: The CAPA Command
requirements.text: When a capability response describes an optional command, the <capa-tag> SHOULD be identical to the command keyword.

requirements.heading: The CAPA Command
requirements.text: Each capability name MAY be followed by a single space and a space-separated list of parameters.

requirements.heading: LOGIN-DELAY capability
requirements.text: Clients which permit the user to configure a mail check interval SHOULD use this capability to determine the minimum permissible interval.

requirements.heading: LOGIN-DELAY capability
requirements.text: Servers which advertise LOGIN- DELAY SHOULD enforce it.

requirements.heading: LOGIN-DELAY capability
requirements.text: If the minimum login delay period could differ per user (that is, the LOGIN-DELAY argument might change after authentication), the server MUST announce in AUTHENTICATION state the largest value which could be set for any user.

requirements.heading: LOGIN-DELAY capability
requirements.text: The server SHOULD append the token "USER" to the LOGIN- DELAY parameter in AUTHENTICATION state, to inform the client that a more accurate value is available after authentication.

requirements.heading: LOGIN-DELAY capability
requirements.text: The server SHOULD announce the more accurate value in TRANSACTION state.

requirements.heading: PIPELINING capability
requirements.text: If a server supports PIPELINING, it MUST process each command in turn.

requirements.heading: PIPELINING capability
requirements.text: If a client uses PIPELINING, it MUST keep track of which commands it has outstanding, and match server responses to commands in order.

requirements.heading: PIPELINING capability
requirements.text: If either the client or server uses blocking writes, it MUST not exceed the window size of the underlying transport layer.

requirements.heading: EXPIRE capability
requirements.text: EXPIRE 0 indicates the client is not permitted to leave mail on the server; when the session enters the UPDATE state the server MAY assume an implicit DELE for each message which was downloaded with RETR.

requirements.heading: EXPIRE capability
requirements.text: If a site uses any automatic deletion policy, it SHOULD use the EXPIRE capability to announce this.

requirements.heading: EXPIRE capability
requirements.text: Sites which permit users to retain messages indefinitely SHOULD announce this with the EXPIRE NEVER response.

requirements.heading: EXPIRE capability
requirements.text: If the expiration policy differs per user (that is, the EXPIRE argument might change after authentication), the server MUST announce in AUTHENTICATION state the smallest value which could be set for any user.

requirements.heading: EXPIRE capability
requirements.text: The server SHOULD append the token "USER" to the EXPIRE parameter in AUTHENTICATION state, to inform the client that a more accurate value is available after authentication.

requirements.heading: IMPLEMENTATION capability
requirements.text: However, a server MAY chose to do so only in TRANSACTION state.

requirements.heading: IMPLEMENTATION capability
requirements.text: A server MAY include the implementation identification both in the welcome banner and in the IMPLEMENTATION capability.

requirements.heading: IMPLEMENTATION capability
requirements.text: Clients MUST NOT modify their behavior based on the server implementation.

requirements.heading: Future Extensions to POP3
requirements.text: Clients MUST NOT require the presence of any extension for basic functionality, with the exception of the authentication commands (APOP, AUTH [section 6.3] and USER/PASS).

requirements.heading: Extended POP3 Response Codes
requirements.text: Clients supporting this extension MAY remove any information enclosed in square brackets prior to displaying human readable text to the user.

requirements.heading: Extended POP3 Response Codes
requirements.text: Clients MUST ignore unknown hierarchical detail about the response code.

requirements.heading: IANA Considerations
requirements.text: New POP3 capabilities MUST be defined in a standards track or IESG approved experimental RFC, and MUST NOT begin with the letter "X".

requirements.heading: IANA Considerations
requirements.text: New POP3 capabilities MUST include the following information: CAPA tag Arguments Added commands Standard commands affected Announced states / possible differences Commands valid in states Specification reference Discussion

requirements.heading: IANA Considerations
requirements.text: New POP3 response codes MUST be defined in an RFC or other permanent and readily available reference, in sufficient detail so that interoperability between independent implementations is possible.

requirements.heading: IANA Considerations
requirements.text: New POP3 response code specifications MUST include the following information: the complete response code, for which responses (+OK or -ERR) and commands it is valid, and a definition of its meaning and expected client behavior.
